summary_of_bug: NumberUtils.createNumber incorrectly rejects uppercase hexadecimal prefixes, throwing NumberFormatException for inputs like "0Xfade" and "-0Xfade" while accepting the lowercase forms "0xFADE" and "-0xFADE". The failing test shows createNumber should parse both 0x and 0X forms equivalently, consistent with Integer.decode behavior described in the bug report.

LANG-710.label: I
LANG-710.reason: This is in `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate` / `StringEscapeUtils`, dealing with HTML numeric entity parsing and an index error in string scanning. The current failure is in `org.apache.commons.lang3.math.NumberUtils.createNumber()` and specifically about recognizing upper-case hex prefixes (`0X`, `-0X`). There is no meaningful regional overlap and the parsing mechanism is different enough to provide essentially no localization signal.
